title: What If the Sun Went Quiet for 70 Years?

scenes.text: What if the Sun went quiet for seventy years? It has done that before.
From 1645 to 1715, the Sun was unusually quiet. That stretch is called the Maunder Minimum.
It overlapped the Little Ice Age, when global temperatures were about one degree Celsius colder than today.
A new one now? Models say it would cool Earth by no more than 0.3 degrees Celsius by 2100.
Greenhouse warming is projected at one to five degrees, so a sleepy Sun would offset only a fraction.
And the cooling would be temporary. A quiet Sun would slow warming, not stop it.
